hero.badge: Christmas quiz • Together, or on your own for your couple
hero.title: The quiz to find out which Christmas characters you are
hero.description: Are you more like Santa and Mrs. Claus or two elves from the workshop? You each answer 12 questions about how you celebrate Christmas. Then the quiz gives you the Christmas duo you make, with its photo.
hero.subtitle: 12 questions • 3 minutes each • on a single phone

section1.title: How the quiz works
section1.p1: This quiz is a Christmas game to play as a couple. It tells you which duo of Christmas characters you make, based on how you spend the holidays. It asks 12 questions about your Christmas. For example, it asks when the decorations come out and what you do on Christmas morning.
section1.p2: Take the question “On Christmas Eve, you are:”. You can choose between “at our place, and we're the ones hosting”, “on the road, between two families”, “just us, in pajamas” and “somewhere with snow”. Each answer gives points to one or two duos. If you answer “at our place”, the quiz gives points to Santa and Mrs. Claus. If you answer “on the road”, it gives points to the two reindeer.
section1.p3: The first person answers the 12 questions and then passes the phone. The second person answers without seeing what the first one chose. Then the quiz adds up your answers and keeps the duo with the most points. It also shows the duo each of you would have got alone and the questions where you gave different answers.
section1.p4: There is one exception. If only one of you answers like someone who's worn out by Christmas, you're Scrooge and the Christmas spirit. In that case, the quiz doesn't look at the points. It's the only duo where the two characters aren't alike!
section1.p5: You can also take the quiz on your own and answer for your couple.

section2.title: The 8 Christmas duos in the quiz
section2.intro: The quiz can give 8 duos and each one has its photo. Here's which couples each duo is most like.

section3.title: Where do these Christmas characters come from?
section3.p1: The Santa everyone knows comes largely from an American poem from 1823 called “A Visit from St. Nicholas”. That poem gave the sleigh its eight reindeer and their names, from Dasher and Dancer to Comet and Cupid.
section3.p2: The Nutcracker comes from a German tale by E. T. A. Hoffmann that dates from 1816. It became a ballet in 1892 with music by Tchaikovsky, and the Sugar Plum Fairy first appears in that ballet. Scrooge is the old miser in “A Christmas Carol”, a story Charles Dickens published in 1843. He hates Christmas until the night three spirits come to visit him.
section3.p3: The Christmas gnomes with long hats come from Scandinavia, where they're called “tomte” or “nisse”. In the stories, they're little creatures who watch over the house. You just have to remember to leave them a bowl of porridge on Christmas Eve!

section4.title: What if you don't celebrate Christmas the same way?
section4.p1: It's very common. For example, one of you grew up with three Christmas dinners and twenty people at the table. The other always had Christmas for four in front of a movie. The quiz shows it right away in the list of questions where you gave different answers.
section4.p2: The simplest thing is to take a bit of each. You keep one tradition from one of you and one from the other, and you make up a new one together. After a few years, those habits show what kind of couple you are.
section4.p3: There's one question this quiz doesn't settle. It doesn't tell you which of you has been nicer this year. There's another quiz for that.

section5.title: Good to know about this quiz
section5.p1: This quiz is a game, just for fun, and it doesn't measure anything serious. You can very well be two Christmas gnomes in December and two reindeer the rest of the year.
section5.p2: Your answers aren't saved, they stay on your phone. We only count which duo you get, to see which results come up most. Your name isn't saved either. The photos were created for this page.

seo.faq1Q: Which Christmas characters can we get?
seo.faq1A: The quiz can give 8 duos: Santa and Mrs. Claus, two elves from the workshop, two of Santa's reindeer, two snowmen, two gingerbread men, the Nutcracker and the Sugar Plum Fairy, Scrooge and the Christmas spirit, and two Christmas gnomes.
seo.faq2A: Each answer gives points to one or two duos. For example, if you answer “we cook for two days, and it's the best part”, the gingerbread men get points. When you take the quiz together, it adds up your answers and the duo with the most points becomes yours.
seo.faq3Q: Can I take the quiz on my own?
seo.faq3A: Yes. Just choose “On my own, for our couple” and answer with your couple in mind. You'll get your duo but you won't be able to compare your answers.
seo.faq4Q: Why are we Scrooge and the Christmas spirit?
seo.faq4A: Because only one of you answered like someone who's worn out by Christmas. For example, that person doesn't get the decorations out and their favorite part is December 26th. In that case, the quiz stops looking at the points and gives you this duo. It also comes up when each of you grumbles.
seo.faq5Q: When should we take this quiz?
seo.faq5A: You can take it in December, for example on the evening when you decorate the tree or on Christmas Eve while waiting for midnight. It takes three minutes each. You can also take it with other couples to compare your duos.
seo.faq6A: No. Your answers stay on your phone. We only count which duo you get, to see which results come up most, and your name isn't saved.
